3.speaker: Elena Werner
3.text: "Surely His Majesty already has some awareness regarding the state of Rizia's economy and resources."

5.speaker: Player_Romus
5.text: "He had the right idea. If Rumburg and the other countries in GRACE stop importing from us, that surplus could disappear."

6.speaker: Elena Werner
6.text: "Thanks to your own wise financial decisions over the past few years, that surplus is fairly high. But of course, there's always room for improvement."

7.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
7.text: "Why would Rumburg suddenly put an end to decades of peaceful trade?"

8.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
8.text: "A shortage of *Rizian* workers, Elena. Those vacancies could easily be filled with migrants from Wehlen and Derdia."

9.speaker: Player_Romus
9.text: "How much of our revenue comes from taxes?"

13.speaker: Player_Romus
13.text: "We don't know how much of Queen Beatrice's goodwill was due to my ties with her sister. With Lena gone, we can't take Rumburg's loyalty for granted."

15.speaker: Player_Romus
15.text: "I trust Rumburg, but it's never wise for a country to rely too much on one trading partner. We need to diversify."

16.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
16.text: "Very astute, Your Majesty. I did have a number of alternative candidates in mind."

17.speaker: Elena Werner
17.text: "For now, are there any other questions?"

19.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
19.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Budget"] == true  or Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Taxes"] == true  or Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gas"] == true

20.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
20.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Budget"] == true  or Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Taxes"] == true  or Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gas"] == true) == false

21.speaker: Player_Romus
21.text: "That's all the information I need for now."
21.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Budget"] == true  or Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Taxes"] == true  or Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gas"] == true

23.speaker: Elena Werner
23.text: "Historically, our resource-based economy has allowed us to have some of the lowest tax rates on the continent. It's been a real boon for businesses."

24.speaker: Player_Romus
24.text: "Watch your words, Ms. Werner. The nobility may not have an income, but we are the foundation upon which Rizian society is built."

25.speaker: Player_Romus
25.text: "That doesn't seem fair. Low-earning workers pay taxes while nobles don't?"

26.speaker: Lucita Azaro
26.text: "Agreed, Your Majesty. Without my family's manufacturing industry investments, for example, half of Cardesse-Montaklar would be out of a job."

27.speaker: Hugo Toras
27.text: "A ten percent tax is a low price for commoners to pay for the privilege of living and working in the best country in Merkopa."

28.speaker: Player_Romus
28.text: "Could we generate extra revenue by introducing estate or inheritance taxes?"

30.speaker: Elena Werner
30.text: "As a fellow monarchy and a member of the Guild of Royal Allies for Commercial Exchange, Rumburg has more than a familial interest in our partnership."

31.speaker: Elena Werner
31.text: "Your House's province, Valenqiris, leads the realm in GDP... driven by its wine, gas, and tourism sectors."

32.speaker: Elena Werner
32.text: "The manufacturing concerns in Cardesse-Montaklar are doing very well, to the point that business councils are complaining about an imminent shortage of skilled workers."

33.speaker: Elena Werner
33.text: "Since we began trading with Rumburg, we've been running a surplus."

37.speaker: Player_Romus
37.text: "Not particularly. I'm the Party Prince, remember?"

38.speaker: Player_Romus
38.text: "We've got gold, we've got energy. What else do I need to know?"

39.speaker: Player_Romus
39.text: "I know the broad strokes. But I'm happy to get caught up on the details."

43.speaker: Player_Romus
43.text: "Yes, but I'm sure my daughter would appreciate a refresher course."

48.speaker: Elena Werner
48.text: "It's slightly more complicated than that, Your Majesty."

50.speaker: Narrator
50.text: She smoothly adjusted her reading glasses before continuing.

51.speaker: Elena Werner
51.text: "Until the 1940s, Rizia was historically one of the wealthiest countries in South Merkopa. But His Majesty the late King Valero bequeathed us a number of challenges in that department."

52.speaker: Elena Werner
52.text: "Or we can spend our budget elsewhere as we wait for access to the new field south of Caleqabiz."

53.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
53.text: "Careful, Ms. Werner. One shouldn't count one's pheasants before they've been bagged."

54.speaker: Player_Romus
54.text: "Excuse me? What field would that be?"

55.speaker: Player_Romus
55.text: "The south of Caleqabiz... wouldn't that put the field close to Pales?"

56.speaker: Player_Romus
56.text: "You will quit squabbling and tell me about this new field at once."

57.speaker: Narrator
57.text: Elena looked at Laurento, then at me.

58.speaker: Elena Werner
58.text: "Well... we're still in the extremely early stages."

59.speaker: Player_Romus
59.text: "What are we waiting for? Let's get to drilling!"

60.speaker: Player_Romus
60.text: "We should proceed very carefully with this. We don't want a gas dispute on our hands."

61.speaker: Player_Romus
61.text: "Perhaps we should let it go, in the interest of keeping the peace with Pales."

63.speaker: Player_Romus
63.text: "You're right, Vina. Duchess Azaro, save the military talk for your own briefing."

64.speaker: Player_Romus
64.text: "Don't interrupt my councilors, Vina. You will speak only when spoken to."

66.speaker: Elena Werner
66.text: "We should save this discussion for if and when we know more about the gas field in question."

67.speaker: Player_Romus
67.text: "Time to grow up, my dear daughter. In real life, there's always a winner and a loser."

68.speaker: Elena Werner
68.text: "But we may have at least part of a claim to a substantial reserve of natural gas between the port of Pales and the Rizian island of Caleqabiz."

70.speaker: Elena Werner
70.text: "Our researchers have been investigating the field's size and borders. Once those are known, it will be easy to determine ownership."

71.speaker: Narrator
71.text: Laurento gave me a significant look.

72.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
72.text: "Exactly, Your Majesty. Ms. Werner, tell him."

73.speaker: Vina Toras
73.text: "I don't know why we're even discussing a military response. We'll surely be able to reach a compromise using proper diplomacy."

83.speaker: Elena Werner
83.text: "It's always a good idea to envision all possible scenarios. But as a fellow monarchy and member of the Guild of Royal Allies for Commercial Exchange, it's against Rumburg's interests to disrupt our partnership."

84.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
84.text: "With that said, your father was conservative when it came to our international trade. I have a number of alternative partners in mind."

85.speaker: Elena Werner
85.text: "Now, new gold mines are scarce, our richest sources nearly depleted, and the Kingdom’s burdens have grown over the past decade."

86.speaker: Player_Romus
86.text: "Do not slander the late King of Rizia. I'm sure my father had his reasons for such frugality."

88.speaker: Elena Werner
88.text: "Indeed not. I'm just pointing out that the money is there, should you choose to spend it."

89.speaker: Player_Romus
89.text: "Nonetheless, it's great to know that we're not going broke."

90.speaker: Player_Romus
90.text: "No need to sugarcoat it. He was a miser."

94.speaker: Player_Romus
94.text: "What's been going on with our gold industry?"

95.speaker: Lucita Azaro
95.text: "With that said, our budget will need more padding if we want to complete the slate of military modernization measures I have in mind."

97.speaker: Elena Werner
97.text: "With all due respect, Duchess Azaro, I'm not sure the military is the King's number one focus."

98.speaker: Player_Romus
98.text: "Why wouldn't it be, Ms. Werner? Rizia continues to have many enemies, both foreign and internal."

100.speaker: Player_Romus
100.text: "It most certainly is not. That money should be spent on the Rizian people, not weapons."

101.speaker: Player_Romus
101.text: "The last time Rizia had a strong military, its members mutinied against us."

103.speaker: Lucita Azaro
103.text: "Very well said, Your Majesty. We cannot rely on the likes of Wehlen or Rumburg to protect us."

104.speaker: Player_Romus
104.text: "No, it isn't. If we invest our surplus in Rizian industries, we'll get back what we spent triplefold."

106.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
106.text: "I agree, Your Majesty. Think of the advances we were able to make during the Lyza era due to the Queen's investments in citizen welfare."

107.speaker: Lucita Azaro
107.text: "That was many years ago, Your Majesty. And the responsible parties have all been punished."

108.speaker: Lucita Azaro
108.text: "Great news, Ms. Werner. I already have a full slate of military modernization measures I was hoping to propose."

109.speaker: Elena Werner
109.text: "He had his reasons, I'm sure. But he did miss a number of potentially lucrative investment opportunities."

110.speaker: Lucita Azaro
110.text: "Including, of course, the opportunity to completely modernize the Rizian military."

111.speaker: Elena Werner
111.text: "Thank you, Mr. Esquibel. You'll get your chance to present those later."

112.speaker: Elena Werner
112.text: "For now, I will point out that holding on to that surplus has not done Rizia any favors. We have missed a number of potentially lucrative investment opportunities."

113.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
113.text: "Ultimately, shouldn't that money be spent on the Rizian people? Think of the advances we were able to make during the Lyza era due to the Queen's investments in citizen welfare."

117.speaker: Vina Toras
117.text: "'True prosperity is not defined by the amount of gold in our coffers, but by the health and happiness of each soul within our borders.'"

118.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
118.text: "I do agree there are better uses for those funds. Think of the advances we were able to make during the Lyza era due to the Queen's investments in citizen welfare."

119.speaker: Player_Romus
119.text: "Shh. You're supposed to be a silent observer."

121.speaker: Player_Romus
121.text: "More pragmatically, a happy and well-fed populace is one that does not rise up against its leaders."

122.speaker: Player_Romus
122.text: "It's true that a happy and well-fed populace is one that does not rise up against its leaders."

123.speaker: Player_Romus
123.text: "On the other hand, there can be no welfare without security. What good is health or happiness if we're unable to defend ourselves?"

124.speaker: Player_Romus
124.text: "Indeed, Mr. Esquibel. If we focus on citizen welfare, we can set the standard not only for Merkopa, but for the world."

126.speaker: Hugo Toras
126.text: "If I may, the Princess has a point. Rizia's wealth, and my mother's judicious handling of it, was one of the factors that allowed us to survive the Century of Revolutions."

127.speaker: Narrator
127.text: Vina blushed and lowered her eyes. Hugo put up a hand.

129.speaker: Narrator
129.text: Vina beamed. Hugo nodded in agreement.

131.speaker: Hugo Toras
131.text: "I will point out that Rizia's wealth, and my mother's judicious handling of it, was one of the factors that allowed us to survive the Century of Revolutions."

133.speaker: Hugo Toras
133.text: "However, those were different times. As a modern nation in an era of increasing superpower influence, we are expected to have a certain standard of military."

134.speaker: Elena Werner
134.text: "Well, Your Majesty, gold is still the backbone of the Rizian economy. Though production has declined as our reserves begin to exhaust themselves."

135.speaker: Elena Werner
135.text: "We can try. There are a number of promising sites that have yet to be explored."

136.speaker: Player_Romus
136.text: "Can't we increase our mining efforts within Rizia to make up for the loss?"
136.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Rizia"] == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Regs"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Zille"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Rizia"] == true) == false)

137.speaker: Elena Werner
137.text: "We have a number of active mines within the country, operated by the Rizian Royal Gold corporation."

138.speaker: Narrator
138.text: She unrolled a map on the table and pointed to a region in the east of Morella.

139.speaker: Elena Werner
139.text: "The double blow of losing our mines in Zille and 15 percent of our RRG stake has made us quite reliant on the gold from the MITZ."

140.speaker: Player_Romus
140.text: "How much say does the government have over operations in the MITZ?"
140.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Regs"] == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Regs"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Zille"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Rizia"] == true) == false)

141.speaker: Elena Werner
141.text: "A fair amount. Any changes to regulations or profit shares have to be agreed on by all four nations involved."

142.speaker: Player_Romus
142.text: "When we get Zille back, will we get its gold back as well?"
142.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Zille"] == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Regs"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Zille"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Rizia"] == true) == false)

143.speaker: Elena Werner
143.text: "I certainly hope so. Wehlen has been mining extensively in the region since taking over in 1927."

158.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
158.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Regs"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Zille"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Rizia"] == true) == false

166.speaker: Elena Werner
166.text: "Very gladly, Your Majesty. This is a new area for us compared to gold, but the financial possibilities are intriguing indeed."

170.speaker: Narrator
170.text: She pointed again at the map on the table, this time directing our attention to the east of Morella.

176.speaker: Narrator
176.text: She pointed at the map in front of her, this time directing our attention to the southern coast of Valenqiris.

177.speaker: Narrator
177.text: She unrolled a map on the table and pointed to the southern coast of Valenqiris.

178.speaker: Elena Werner
178.text: "Though our state energy company is called Rizian Oil and Gas, production of the former has slowed over the years, and is threatening to come to a complete halt. The latter, however, shows immense potential."

179.speaker: Elena Werner
179.text: "Our most productive gas field is Esqiris, off the coast of Topes. Assuming enough money is invested into its expansion, we can expect it to fuel our kingdom for years to come."

182.speaker: Lucita Azaro
182.text: "Forgive me, Your Majesty. I thought you were asking for my input."

185.speaker: Elena Werner
185.text: "That's it for our discussion on gold. Shall we move on?"

187.speaker: Elena Werner
187.text: "The central government does collect a flat income tax of ten percent. This is mostly paid by workers, since nobles have no income to speak of."

188.speaker: Elena Werner
188.text: "I didn't make the rules, Your Majesty. They were proposed by the House of Delegates and agreed on by your father."

190.speaker: Elena Werner
190.text: "I do happen to think that taxing wealthy nobles makes more sense than taxing the workers who generate said wealth."

191.speaker: Elena Werner
191.text: "On the other hand, the current tax code was proposed by the House of Delegates and agreed on by your father. It might not be easy to change it."

193.speaker: Elena Werner
193.text: "Compared to most of our neighbors, yes. We do provide a high standard of social services to our people, but it's mostly financed with trade income."

194.speaker: Hugo Toras
194.text: "This is by the House of Delegates' design, Your Majesty. Lowering the tax burden on citizens leads to higher satisfaction with the government and less likelihood of rebellion."

196.speaker: Hugo Toras
196.text: "The commoners should consider themselves lucky. Ten percent is far lower than elsewhere."

197.speaker: Hugo Toras
197.text: "Nor should we. Taxing nobles would be an attack on the very backbone of Rizian society."

198.speaker: Lucita Azaro
198.text: "Yes, our families' investments power half the businesses in this country. Why should we be forced to pay double?"

199.speaker: Player_Romus
199.text: "But nobles only got the money for those investments by siphoning it from hard-working commoners. Isn't it our responsibility to break the cycle somehow?"

200.speaker: Player_Romus
200.text: "You have a point. We shouldn't disincentivize families like yours from supporting Rizia's economy."

201.speaker: Player_Romus
201.text: "I'm still not convinced. But I'll drop the subject for now."

202.speaker: Player_Romus
202.text: "I still think that rate could be higher. Imagine what we could do with the funding!"

203.speaker: Player_Romus
203.text: "A wise idea. But it leaves us at the mercy of our resources and trade partners."

204.speaker: Player_Romus
204.text: "I understand. We certainly don't want another uprising."

205.speaker: Lucita Azaro
205.text: "And our family's investments power half of Rizia's businesses anyway. Why ask us to pay double?"

206.speaker: Hugo Toras
206.text: "I don't think it would be wise. The House of Delegates determined that lowering the tax burden on citizens leads to higher satisfaction with the government and less likelihood of rebellion."

207.speaker: Player_Romus
207.text: "It's no wonder there hasn't been another uprising when they're paying that little."

209.speaker: Player_Romus
209.text: "Why not get rid of income tax altogether, then?"

210.speaker: Hugo Toras
210.text: "Yes, this was the House of Delegates' intention. Lowering the tax burden on citizens leads to higher satisfaction with the government and less likelihood of rebellion."

211.speaker: Player_Romus
211.text: "I do wonder if the nobility should contribute more. We can certainly afford to."

212.speaker: Hugo Toras
212.text: "If you'd like to retain the loyalty of the House of Delegates, I would suggest keeping our tax laws the way they are."

213.speaker: Elena Werner
213.text: "That would be a risk, Your Majesty. Without any other revenue-generating measure to replace that tax, it would leave us completely reliant on our natural resources."

214.speaker: Elena Werner
214.text: "We already have a budget surplus, Your Majesty. I see no need to raise taxes unless it's absolutely necessary."

215.speaker: Elena Werner
215.text: "Not completely. But yes, if our international trade were to be disrupted, we would have to abandon this system."

216.speaker: Elena Werner
216.text: "At the moment, we have little risk of that."

218.speaker: Hugo Toras
218.text: "It is our responsibility to make wise choices with the money we have. Dwelling on how we came to have it accomplishes nothing."

219.speaker: Hugo Toras
219.text: "Think of your own house, Your Majesty. Would the Rizian wine industry be where it is without our backing?"

220.speaker: Elena Werner
220.text: "Very well, Your Majesty. For the record, I'm not convinced either."

221.speaker: Elena Werner
221.text: "In terms of our provinces' individual contributions... they pay less than three percent directly to the Crown, which mostly goes towards administrative costs."

222.speaker: Elena Werner
222.text: "Brenas is still suffering the effects of the loss of Iza and Zille. However, it's made advances in shipping and agriculture, alongside its gold mines."

223.speaker: Hugo Toras
223.text: "That is a slippery slope, Mr. Esquibel."

224.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
224.text: "After the Wehlen Civil War, we began granting 'labor hand' visas to Wehzek migrants and a smaller number of Derdians."

225.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
225.text: "Are you familiar with Rizia's two-tier employment system, Your Majesty?"

228.speaker: Elena Werner
228.text: "Labor hands may accept employment by Rizian industries, but they don't have the right to social security or other benefits. And there is a cap on how much they are allowed to earn."

229.speaker: Elena Werner
229.text: "They now make up most of our blue-collar workforce, with higher-paid jobs held by native Rizians as well as smaller numbers of Lespians, Valgslandians and Rumburgians."

230.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
230.text: "The program did wonders for the economy when King Valero initiated it. But as a result, we now have millions of workers in this country who are being treated like second-class citizens."

231.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
231.text: "Granting 'labor hand' visas to Wehzeks and Derdians did wonders for our economy in the 1930s and 40s."

232.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
232.text: "But as a result, Rizia now has a millions-strong workforce that is essentially treated like second-class citizens."

233.speaker: Player_Romus
233.text: "They should have the same working rights as their Rizian counterparts. Especially if they're paying taxes."

234.speaker: Player_Romus
234.text: "If the system functions, I see no need to change it."

235.speaker: Player_Romus
235.text: "Those visas were granted to temporary residents. They were supposed to go home at some point."

236.speaker: Player_Romus
236.text: "I see where you're going with this, but granting them full employment rights would lead to a flood of uncontrolled migration."

237.speaker: Hugo Toras
237.text: "Rizia offered Wehzeks asylum where other countries did not. There must be some limit to our generosity."

238.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
238.text: "I wouldn't say it functions. Barring these people from upward mobility will have consequences in the long term. The worker shortage Elena mentioned is just one of those."

239.speaker: Elena Werner
239.text: "That was the initial aim. But Rizia's current-day economy now relies on these workers."

240.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
240.text: "All the more reason why they deserve an upgrade in status."

241.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
241.text: "I'm not sure about that. The situation in Wehlen has stabilized since the Civil War."

245.speaker: Hugo Toras
245.text: "There was a time when you supported that stance, Your Majesty."

246.speaker: Player_Romus
246.text: "I'm just being pragmatic. Expanding foreign workers' rights does seem like a convenient solution to the shortage Elena mentioned."

247.speaker: Hugo Toras
247.text: "Rizia offered Wehzeks asylum where other countries did not. There must be some limit to our generosity."

251.speaker: Hugo Toras
251.text: "I recall you once supported that stance as well, Your Majesty."

252.speaker: Player_Romus
252.text: "I was a different person back in those days. I no longer support Su Omina or the values it stands for."

253.speaker: Player_Romus
253.text: "I did and I still do. I'm all for diversity, but we Rizians cannot allow ourselves to become outnumbered."

254.speaker: Player_Romus
254.text: "Taking advantage of migrants' dire financial situation by forcing them to work for low wages is hardly 'generosity.'"

255.speaker: Player_Romus
255.text: "From a purely pragmatic point of view, expanding foreign workers' rights does seem like a convenient solution to the shortage Elena mentioned."

256.speaker: Player_Romus
256.text: "Perhaps. But I do worry that having a growing army of disenfranchised laborers will lead to unrest down the line."

257.speaker: Player_Romus
257.text: "Exactly. I'm all for diversity, but we Rizians cannot allow ourselves to become outnumbered."

258.speaker: Lucita Azaro
258.text: "From a security standpoint, allowing migrants to earn more money would curb the kind of black-market activities that have been taking place in cities like Iza."

259.speaker: Lucita Azaro
259.text: "Very possible, Your Majesty. And allowing migrants to earn more money would curb the kind of black-market activities that have been taking place in cities like Iza."

260.speaker: Lucita Azaro
260.text: "And from a security standpoint, allowing migrants to earn more money would curb the kind of black-market activities that have been taking place in cities like Iza."

261.speaker: Hugo Toras
261.text: "Do you not fear the dilution of Rizian culture and values, Duchess Azaro? Or the infiltration of Dastnurists and Golcondists into our Wruhecist society?"

263.speaker: Lucita Azaro
263.text: "Societies change, Your Grace. And I don't recall these concerns being raised about the Rumburgians who moved here after our alliance."

264.speaker: Lucita Azaro
264.text: "I will add that from a security standpoint, allowing migrants to earn more money would curb the kind of black-market activities that have been taking place in cities like Iza."

265.speaker: Lucita Azaro
265.text: "I will point out that from a security standpoint, allowing migrants to earn more money would curb the kind of black-market activities that have been taking place in cities like Iza."

266.speaker: Player_Romus
266.text: "Well put, Duchess. I can already tell you're going to be a brilliant addition to this council."

267.speaker: Player_Romus
267.text: "That's completely different. The Rumburgians are our blood relations."

268.speaker: Player_Romus
268.text: "To tell the truth, I'm not thrilled about any of those groups."

269.speaker: Player_Romus
269.text: "Rizia is a multicultural nation now, Hugo. Whether we like it or not."

271.speaker: Narrator
271.text: I saw a smile play across her lips. Hugo stayed silent.

272.speaker: Hugo Toras
272.text: "There are also far fewer of them."

273.speaker: Hugo Toras
273.text: "Nor am I. But the Rumburgians are a small minority compared to the Wehzeks."

274.speaker: Hugo Toras
274.text: "We cannot let the events of the last two decades destroy what it has taken over a thousand years to build."

275.speaker: Narrator
275.text: Hugo fixed Lucita with a defiant stare.

276.speaker: Elena Werner
276.text: "We seem to have veered off track. Can we get back to your questions about the economy?"

277.speaker: Narrator
277.text: Elena looked uneasily at the three of us. She tapped a pencil on the table.

279.speaker: Player_Romus
279.text: "You're right, Hugo. I'll take Duchess Azaro's suggestion seriously."

280.speaker: Player_Romus
280.text: "Other countries might compete to have the biggest guns. Not Rizia."

281.speaker: Player_Romus
281.text: "And there's the fact that we're sandwiched between the highly contentious regions of Zille and Pales."

282.speaker: Player_Romus
282.text: "If we cultivate our alliances well, we won't need that."

284.speaker: Lucita Azaro
284.text: "It's not about big guns, Your Majesty. It's about being prepared for any eventuality."

285.speaker: Lucita Azaro
285.text: "Precisely, Your Majesty. We've got to be prepared for the worst-case scenario, even if it doesn't happen."

286.speaker: Lucita Azaro
286.text: "Allies can turn on us, Your Majesty. A loyal, well-funded military is worth its weight in gold."

287.speaker: Elena Werner
287.text: "Your enthusiasm is heartening, Duchess Azaro. I'm sure you'll have much more advice to share during your own briefing."

295.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
295.text: "It was established shortly before you joined the Royal Council, was it not, Elena? I heard the negotiations between Rizia, Valgsland, Lespia and Morella took over a year."

296.speaker: Elena Werner
296.text: "We would just need to commission a survey to find them. Keeping in mind that any mining site near noble-owned estates might lead to a devaluation of those properties."

297.speaker: Elena Werner
297.text: "But as per the terms of our agreement, Zille and all of the resources therein will return to Rizian ownership in 1952."

299.speaker: Narrator
299.text: Laurento looked down at the table.

300.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
300.text: "Forgive me, Your Majesty. I will let the treasurer speak."

301.speaker: Elena Werner
301.text: "I'd like nothing more, Your Majesty. But protocol must be followed."

302.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
302.text: "Of course, we are liaising extremely closely with Pales to avoid misunderstandings."

303.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
303.text: "I agree that maintaining or even improving our relations with Pales should be our number-one goal."

307.speaker: Player_Romus
307.text: "Pales barely counts as a country. Of course we have a claim to the field."

309.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
309.text: "Whatever our feelings about Palesian sovereignty, we are bound to respect protocol."

310.speaker: Elena Werner
310.text: "We have teamed up with Palesian researchers to investigate the field's size and borders. Once those are known, it will be easier to determine ownership."

311.speaker: Elena Werner
311.text: "With that said, if there's even a chance we have a claim to that gas, we really ought to take it."

312.speaker: Lucita Azaro
312.text: "As we should. Nobody wants a repeat of the last conflict."

313.speaker: Player_Romus
313.text: "Really, Duchess Azaro? Your family isn't itching for a rematch?"

314.speaker: Player_Romus
314.text: "If it *does* come down to that -- God forbid -- Rizia will win."

315.speaker: Player_Romus
315.text: "Indeed not. I will not practice the same mindless militarism as my father and Taddeus Azaro."

319.speaker: Player_Romus
319.text: "If the Grand Duchy does not provoke us, we will not provoke them."

321.speaker: Lucita Azaro
321.text: "Just because the Azaros are demanding the reclamation of Pales doesn't mean it's a good idea."

322.speaker: Lucita Azaro
322.text: "Of course, if Pales shows hostility towards us, we will react in kind. But Rizia should not be the first to resort to aggression."

324.speaker: Lucita Azaro
324.text: "Not with our military in its current state."

325.speaker: Lucita Azaro
325.text: "As much as my family is clamoring for a repeat of the Pales campaign, I think it's best to ignore them."

327.speaker: Lucita Azaro
327.text: "The attack on Pales in the '20s was not 'mindless', Your Majesty. It was driven by demand from the people."

328.speaker: Lucita Azaro
328.text: "But some people don't know what's best for them. Especially my family."

330.speaker: Lucita Azaro
330.text: "As much as my family is clamoring for a repeat of the Pales campaign, I think it's best to ignore them."

332.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
332.text: "'True prosperity is not defined by the amount of gold in our coffers, but by the health and happiness of each soul within our borders.'"

334.speaker: Hugo Toras
334.text: "The people of this country will accept diversity up to a certain point, Your Majesty. But if they begin to feel their national identity is under threat, there will be consequences."

336.speaker: Hugo Toras
336.text: "And unfortunately, we cannot talk about Rizian Royal Gold without talking about its CEO."

337.speaker: Player_Romus
337.text: "Why do we have to talk about him? It's Rizian *Royal* Gold, after all."

339.speaker: Player_Romus
339.text: "We had better get that discussion over with."

340.speaker: Player_Romus
340.text: "Do not speak ill of our country's most vaunted businessman."

341.speaker: Hugo Toras
341.text: "My apologies, Your Majesty. Of course I do not mean to call Russello Montoro's acumen into question."

342.speaker: Elena Werner
342.text: "That's the problem. It isn't ours. Since 1935, it's been under the control of Russello Montoro."

343.speaker: Elena Werner
343.text: "Your uncle never could countenance the presence of Russello Montoro. But we can't mine gold in this country without him."

344.speaker: Elena Werner
344.text: "For better or worse, our country's gold stores rely on Russello Montoro."

345.speaker: Player_Romus
345.text: "I still cannot believe he was allowed to gain such a large majority."

346.speaker: Elena Werner
346.text: "After a *very* lengthy back-and-forth, it was agreed that the Kingdom's share in RRG be decreased from 45 to 30 percent."

347.speaker: Elena Werner
347.text: "Mr. Montoro -- excuse me, Rusty -- currently owns 70 percent of Rizian Royal Gold."

348.speaker: Player_Romus
348.text: "That's fine by me. We all know that private enterprise can achieve what the government cannot."

349.speaker: Player_Romus
349.text: "As much as I respect Rusty, I believe we royals should be in charge of our own gold mines."

352.speaker: Elena Werner
352.text: "Rusty's first move after taking over the company was to sue your father's government for loss of revenue connected to the Zille handover."

353.speaker: Hugo Toras
353.text: "In some cases, perhaps. But after what this man did..."

355.speaker: Player_Romus
355.text: "I will not tolerate this. I want Rizia's original stake back."

356.speaker: Player_Romus
356.text: "Rizia should not own 30 percent of RRG, or even 45 percent. The entire company should be nationalized."

357.speaker: Player_Romus
357.text: "I don't see any problem with that. We shouldn't have so much of our money tied up in an outdated resource."

358.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
358.text: "I beg your pardon, Your Majesty, but healthy gold stocks are crucial to Rizia's reputation on the international stage."

359.speaker: Elena Werner
359.text: "Rumburg is buying our gold for technological uses. And some of our neighbors have shown interest in using it to shore up their unstable currencies, as we did here after the '26 uprising."

361.speaker: Elena Werner
361.text: "Curry enough favor with Rusty, and it should be possible. But any more than 45 percent will be difficult."

362.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
362.text: "The patent for RRG's proprietary mining technology was filed in Ventrie City, Arcasia. And most of its financial assets are kept in Kyrute."

363.speaker: Elena Werner
363.text: "In other words, attempting to nationalize the company without Mr. Montoro's express approval would strip it of its value."

364.speaker: Narrator
364.text: She adjusted her glasses before continuing.

365.speaker: Elena Werner
365.text: "While RRG controls mining within Rizia, the royal government is a direct stakeholder in the Meftiem International Trade Zone."

366.speaker: Elena Werner
366.text: "And at the time of our last survey, there was much more than 30 years' worth of gold in the ground there."

367.speaker: Narrator
367.text: I saw Hugo wince at that remark.

368.speaker: Elena Werner
368.text: "RRG gets a percentage of the MITZ profits for the use of its technology, but we can make decisions without Mr. Montoro's input."

370.speaker: Player_Romus
370.text: "I get the picture. Let's move on to other topics."
370.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Regs"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Zille"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Econ_Gold_Rizia"] == true) == false

374.speaker: Hugo Toras
374.text: "Which, by the way, is why I wholeheartedly support your decision to impose a tax on non-Wruhecists so early into your reign."

375.speaker: Hugo Toras
375.text: "Which, by the way, is why I wholeheartedly support the Rizian National Coalition's suggestion to impose a tax on non-Wruhecists. Filling our coffers and rewarding the native Rizian faithful in one go."

379.speaker: Elena Werner
379.text: "It's not as high as it used to be. But I think we should put it to work."

383.speaker: Lucita Azaro
383.text: "I'm sure His Majesty will agree with me."

384.speaker: Player_Romus
384.text: "I share your goals, Duchess. By the end of my reign, the Rizian Armed Forces shall be known and feared throughout the continent."

386.speaker: Lucita Azaro
386.text: "I've planned a separate meeting to discuss national security. We'll go over it all then."

387.speaker: Player_Romus
387.text: "Enhancing our army stockpiles will be good for Rizia's finances, Ms. Werner. If there's one thing there's always a market for, it's weapons."

388.speaker: Elena Werner
388.text: "Hmm. You do have a point there."

389.speaker: Lucita Azaro
389.text: "As long as we've got enough left over to fight with if need be."

390.speaker: Player_Romus
390.text: "I chose to gave our military a much-needed upgrade before my coronation, yes. That doesn't mean it will be a major focus during my reign."

392.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
392.text: "Not that I disagree with King Romus, but I personally believe that more financial attention should be paid to our citizens' welfare."

393.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
393.text: "Doing so would vastly improve our global image. You'll remember Queen Lyza's famous quote..."

398.speaker: Elena Werner
398.text: "I believe you know the answer, Your Majesty."

402.speaker: Elena Werner
402.text: "Your past efforts have certainly helped bolster our reserves. However, the amount of gold in the ground is finite, and extraction has plateaued."

403.speaker: Elena Werner
403.text: "Very gladly, Your Majesty. I know this is your area of expertise, but there have been a few new developments."

407.speaker: Elena Werner
407.text: "Said surplus is... unusually large, compared to your father's regime. It's almost as if you've been able to conjure up money out of nowhere."

408.speaker: Player_Romus
408.text: "I do, Ms. Werner. As a matter of fact, there's no need for today's briefing. Why don't you all take the rest of the day off?"

409.speaker: Narrator
409.text: My councilors glanced at each other in surprise.

411.speaker: Player_Romus
411.text: "I find I think best when I'm alone. Get me in my study with a fountain pen and a stack of decrees, and I'll handle the rest."

415.speaker: Elena Werner
415.text: "Perhaps you're all caught up on our economic situation, but Her Highness still has much to learn."

416.speaker: Player_Romus
416.text: "Very well. For Vina's sake, please proceed."

417.speaker: Player_Romus
417.text: "The Lord will guide me to make the right decisions, Elena. Your counsel is not necessary."

418.speaker: Player_Romus
418.text: "And learn she will. Vina, this is how a real king cuts through the blather and gets down to business."

419.speaker: Player_Romus
419.text: "You clearly worked hard to put today's briefing together. So please proceed."

421.speaker: Narrator
421.text: Elena frowned, clearly hurt, before straightening up and snapping her ledger shut.

422.speaker: Narrator
422.text: Vina stared at me in confusion. A faint smile of amusement played on Lucita's lips.

424.speaker: Player_Romus
424.text: "Get some fresh air. Cut loose a little. It's not like you're getting any younger."

425.speaker: Narrator
425.text: A faint smile of amusement played on Lucita's lips.

427.speaker: Elena Werner
427.text: "I understand. I won't get in your way, then."

429.speaker: Elena Werner
429.text: "The arrangement dates back to agreements made after the War of Rizian Succession. After four years of civil war, the Crown granted broad fiscal autonomy to the provinces."

430.speaker: Hugo Toras
430.text: "It is the very structure of the realm, our code of agreements, one that has endured for centuries. The provinces remain the backbone of the kingdom."

431.speaker: Player_Romus
431.text: "I want to know what returns we’re getting through growth."

432.speaker: Player_Romus
432.text: "Then let’s go over what each province contributes."

434.speaker: Elena Werner
434.text: "There are key differences worth your attention. Let me walk you through them."

435.speaker: Elena Werner
435.text: "Of course. Their profiles vary, but each plays a big role."

436.speaker: Elena Werner
436.text: "Growth, trade, and indirect levies offer us some leverage. Let me break it down."

437.speaker: Elena Werner
437.text: "All glory to the late Valero, but he had a certain prudence about spending government funds, even when it might have made Rizia richer today."
